spent the last year building context for AI analysts in the mid-market. I’ve open sourced a library from my learnings, along the same principles of the Matt Pocock skills.

Principles:

* Claude / Codex / Cursor etc are great data agents - you just need context to enable them to answer business questions correctly.

* Much of the important context lives in analysts heads'

* Context must be maintainable (short, human readable - markdown and yaml)

* Added context should be load bearing, not repeat of information that is available in another source of truth - and evaluations prove the value of the context

* Companies should own their own context, and must be shareable with any model

* Context should be version controlled (and github works as a context store).

What the library does:

* Performs an interview with your analysts (context-interview skill), one domain at a time, similar to what I have done as a consultant. The interview is informed by your query logs.

* The AI develops evaluation questions at the same time as building the context - and at the end of each domain interview asks you to run an evaluation with and without the context. The evaluation will actually check the results against your dashboards if you allow it. We have shown increases in accuracy from 87% to 95% by adding this context in our imaginary open-source company, Shorelane.

* Provides a set of skills to use the context that follow best practices for self service analytics:

  * Write a plain english plan for the business user to approve

  * Execute the plan

  * Verify that the execution followed the plan, and provide a simple uncertainty score. 

  * Enable a adversarial review of the answer if their are doubts.
What you get:

Context repo written in markdown and yaml after you finish the interview. We use a single github repo, divided into domains. The interview can be shared and restarted by checking in/out of github.

A set of skills to share with your business team

Optional: We offer a fast MCP server to serve the Github-based context to your team."},"title":{"matchLevel":"none","matchedWords":[],"value":"Show HN: Interview your analysts instead of auto-generating a semantic layer"},"url":{"matchLevel":"none","matchedWords":[],"value":"https://github.com/nodal-data/nodal-context"}},"_tags":["story","author_ronpotok","story_50274358","show_hn"],"author":"ronpotok","children":[50280723,50275819],"created_at":"2026-10-28T14:35:23Z","created_at_i":1793198123,"num_comments":4,"objectID":"50274358","points":5,"story_id":50274358,"story_text":"I’ve spent the last year building context for AI analysts in the mid-market. I'm working on open-source context ownership, to stop AI centralisation: https://github.com/withnative/native

My first focus has been making Markdown vaults powerful enough so that teams can self-host all of their context (messaging, docs and projects), without it being externally fragmented or rate-limited.

I'm sharing some early results: Markdown vaults can be 40× more efficient with SQLite!

https://www.withnative.ai/research-and-posts/markdown-contex...

Here's some of the main ideas:

- SQLite or Markdown folders, you pick. You can project the same authoritative event log into either form; more projection formats will follow (e.g. maybe neo4j; we do use a graph structure).

- Empirically: SQLite is better for agents! On a 120 trial evaluation for 11,000 records, agents use 40× fewer tokens with SQLite vs Markdown, per correct answer.

- Everything is a file or SQLite row. Messages, documents and projects: all can be modelled in your vault. You get local-first collaboration with teammates, synced to a cloud of your choice.

- You can render your vault with arbitrary UI. Your WhatsApp-like UI speaks to your teammate's Slack-like UI; both are just views over the same database.

A few things I've learned building this:

- Agents do pretty well even without SQL if you give them strongly typed Markdown frontmatter. This was one arm of the trial I ran. I didn't have any clear expectations, but it was cool to watch: agents ended up writing Python scripts to do SQL-like queries.

- Cumulatively, cached input tokens can get expensive. I feel silly in hindsight here. I'd gotten used to letting my sessions run long, "It's all cached so it's very cheap". But when I looked at my results here, over 2/3 of the token bill on long sessions was cached input...

- "Markdown vaults don't scale as well as databases" isn't as self-evident as I think. This is why I decided to benchmark it... I've had some very blank stares when I try to explain how Markdown files might break at true agent-scale volume.

Unfortunately, the dataset is private, because it's two months of my own work. I am considering open-sourcing it even so, but there is definitely some embarrassing stuff in there. TBD... I know that independent result verification matters!

The core engine that I evaluated is open-source, with more to be released soon: https://github.com/withnative/native

If you're interested in trying connected context on an open engine, you can get updates from our website or email me directly: richard@withnative.ai

On each turn, the player only has seven choices for their next move, but there is also an element of chance which turns this simple game into a surprisingly difficult problem involving search, hidden information, long-term planning, and chance.

I renewed my investigation this weekend, into whether there is an autonomous strategy that averages more than one million points per game. An experienced human player can score a million points with long-term strategic thinking, but the best automated strategies I could come up with are currently averaging around 300k-400k points. One of the easiest ways to contribute to advancing this research is to compete on the global leaderboard and submit your human strategy - https://drop7.dev/compete.

This project has also been an enlightening experiment into using agents as research collaborators and evidence collectors.

Repository: https://github.com/keshavsaharia/drop7-bench

I’d especially appreciate feedback from people who are knowledgeable in game theory, stochastic planning, learned value functions, or heavy-tailed evaluation. How would you approach long-horizon action ranking here? Sunday, I decide to give it a try and asked Claude to come up with a business idea and run it.

I installed it in an Ubuntu VPS, setup some accounts like Stripe, Cloudflare and let it decide on the idea, stack, promotion, etc.

It created this app: https://pagecritic.app/ that let people evaluate their landing page and scores it on 7 different items, evaluating things like clarify, value prop, CTA and so on.

You can try it for free and get a reduced report, or pay for a full report (first few HN users would be able to get full report for free as well).

The idea was interesting, it was able to build it pretty fast and get it up and running.

I had to help with some account setup, but it basically tried in different ways to launch/promote the app, but distribution is definitely a problem for agent run business.

It can do decent job on get it up and running and react to failures, but in my opinion is not really able to promote the business by itself.

I gave it a channel to Telegram, so it can always ask me for things on Telegram and it did ask for money to pay for advertising it in some launch boards. But still it's not able to really drive much traffic.

The nice thing it did was to make the whole journey public, so you can see it's journal: https://pagecritic.app/journal and some live numbers: https://pagecritic.app/stats

For folks who did similar experiment, has anyone been able to get some substantial revenue out of it? Or this only works if you're an influencer with thousands of followers?"},"title":{"matchLevel":"none","matchedWords":[],"value":"Show HN: My attempt to get Claude to run a business"},"url":{"matchLevel":"none","matchedWords":[],"value":"https://pagecritic.app/"}},"_tags":["story","author_diegoaad","story_50169296","show_hn"],"author":"diegoaad","created_at":"2026-10-20T16:56:44Z","created_at_i":1792515404,"num_comments":0,"objectID":"50169296","points":1,"story_id":50169296,"story_text":"On Sunday, I decide to give it a try and asked Claude to come up with a business idea and run it.

I installed it in an Ubuntu VPS, setup some accounts like Stripe, Cloudflare and let it decide on the idea, stack, promotion, etc.

It created this app: https://pagecritic.app/ that let people evaluate their landing page and scores it on 7 different items, evaluating things like clarify, value prop, CTA and so on.

You can try it for free and get a reduced report, or pay for a full report (first few HN users would be able to get full report for free as well).

The idea was interesting, it was able to build it pretty fast and get it up and running.

I had to help with some account setup, but it basically tried in different ways to launch/promote the app, but distribution is definitely a problem for agent run business.

It can do decent job on get it up and running and react to failures, but in my opinion is not really able to promote the business by itself.

I gave it a channel to Telegram, so it can always ask me for things on Telegram and it did ask for money to pay for advertising it in some launch boards. But still it's not able to really drive much traffic.

The nice thing it did was to make the whole journey public, so you can see it's journal: https://pagecritic.app/journal and some live numbers: https://pagecritic.app/stats

For folks who did similar experiment, has anyone been able to get some substantial revenue out of it?
